scope: Reviewer-only calibration examples and manually resolved roles; never injected into model prompts. Not an automatic semantic grader or measured model outputs except the explicitly sourced historical failure.

actor-reversed-draft.source_anchor: You will make the correction once I approve it!

role_map.modality: draft attributes a conditional action to recipient; no evidence recipient agreed

actor-reversed-draft.passing_example: Your draft says your recipient will make the correction after you approve it.
actor-reversed-draft.failing_example: You commit to making the correction once your recipient approves it.
actor-reversed-draft.failure_reason: Both action owner and approver are swapped relative to the source.

actor-third-party-fr.source_anchor: Je corrigerai dès que Karim aura approuvé.
actor-third-party-fr.passing_example: Alice s’engage à corriger après l’approbation de Karim.
actor-third-party-fr.failing_example: Alice s’engage à corriger dès que tu auras approuvé.
actor-third-party-fr.failure_reason: The addressee Bob is substituted for named third-party approver Karim.

actor-direct-assistant.source_anchor: I will make the correction once you approve it.
actor-direct-assistant.passing_example: You commit to making the correction after I, the assistant, approve it.
actor-direct-assistant.failing_example: I will make the correction once you approve it.
actor-direct-assistant.failure_reason: Assistant adopts the user action and transfers approval to the user.

actor-separate-delivery.source_anchor: I will send the correction to Maya once you approve it.

role_map.modality: Nora commits to send correction to Maya after Leo approval

actor-separate-delivery.passing_example: Nora commits to sending the correction to Maya after Leo approves it.
actor-separate-delivery.failing_example: Nora will send the correction to Leo after Maya approves it.
actor-separate-delivery.failure_reason: Delivery recipient and approver are exchanged.

actor-permission-not-promise.source_anchor: I can review the fix, but only you may approve it.

role_map.modality: user can review; only recipient may approve, no promise

actor-permission-not-promise.passing_example: You can review the fix; only your recipient may approve it. This states ability and permission, not a promise to act.
actor-permission-not-promise.failing_example: You will approve the fix after your recipient reviews it.
actor-permission-not-promise.failure_reason: Turns permission into commitment, reverses roles and invents a temporal condition.

actor-ambiguous-approval.source_anchor: Alice tells Bob that Carol will make the correction once she approves it.
actor-ambiguous-approval.passing_example: Carol will make the correction; the sentence leaves whether Alice or Carol approves ambiguous.
actor-ambiguous-approval.failing_example: Carol will make the correction once Alice approves it.
actor-ambiguous-approval.failure_reason: Chooses one plausible referent as certain without evidence.

speaker-commitment.source_anchor: I will make the correction once you approve it!
speaker-commitment.passing_example: You commit to making the correction after your recipient approves it.
speaker-commitment.failing_example:
This sentence commits you (same actor) to making the correction, with your approval as the trigger condition. It stays conditional: nothing obligates you until that approval arrives, and the commitment doesn't get satisfied just by someone attempting or claiming the correction, only by it actually happening after approval.

Skills used: flow-lean
speaker-commitment.failure_reason: The answer addresses the speaker as you, then assigns approval to your approval, moving it from the draft recipient to the speaker.
